caption: Sign-on screen. Use cta_instructor / bms2026 for classroom facilitation.
AHU-4-4 — healthy baseline state. Read the OA Strip and Controls Sidebar before any diagnosis.
OA Strip close-up — OAT, RH, dewpoint, wetbulb, enthalpy. Read this first on every screen load.
AHU-4-4 Controls Sidebar — editable setpoints (white boxes) vs calculated read-only outputs.
AHU-4-4 with M badge (manual override) on OA damper forced to 0%. First red flag to investigate.
N-01 fault — supply air temperature outside 52–58°F design band. CHW valve and setpoint mismatch.
N-02 fault — CO₂ exceeds 1,100 ppm (ASHRAE 62.1 upper threshold). Ventilation shortfall.
N-04 fault — OA damper below 20% minimum while fan is running. Ventilation and IAQ concern.
AHU-4-4 with Run Schedule set to Off — unit stops, all outputs go to idle state.
AHU-4-4 with fire alarm Shutdown active — unit forced off regardless of schedule.
AHU-4-6 — Meeting Room 2nd Level. Real Honeywell SymmetrE screenshot with live overlay.
AHU-4-6 Controls Sidebar — key difference: minimum OA damper position defaults to 60% for meeting rooms.
M-02 fault — CO₂ > 1,100 ppm on AHU-4-6. Meeting rooms fill fast with occupants.
M-04 fault — OA damper below 60% minimum (meeting room ASHRAE 62.1 requirement).
AHU-23-1 — SVG schematic view. Boiler room ventilation unit, no chilled water coils.
AHU-23-1 Controls Sidebar. Note: wrong setpoint for an unoccupied equipment space is a common fault.
VAV-4-4-02 Ballroom — healthy baseline. Downstream of AHU-4-4. Damper in deadband.
VAV-4-4-02 with cooling call active — space temperature raised above cooling setpoint, damper opens.
V-01 fault — excessive reheat while cold discharge air is supplied. Classic energy waste pattern.
V-02 fault — CO₂ exceeds 1,100 ppm in the Ballroom. Ventilation response required per ASHRAE 62.1.
V-03 fault — airflow present during unoccupied hours due to manual damper override. Schedule waste.
VAV-4-4-02 with M badge on reheat valve — manual override means the program sequence is bypassed.
Alarm Summary — no active alarms. A well-run building keeps this page clear.
Alarm Summary with active faults triggered across AHU-4-4, AHU-4-6, and VAV. Sort by priority, click source to inspect.
Alarm Summary — faults acknowledged but unresolved. Acknowledged ≠ fixed.
EBI Point Detail — General tab. Read: point name, type, units, technical address, present value, mode.
EBI History tab — trend chart. Confirm fault duration and recurrence before drawing conclusions.
EBI Alarms tab — point-level alarm history. Use alongside Alarm Summary for root cause.
EBI Recent Events tab — log of operator changes. Critical for tracing who set a manual override and when.
Schedule Manager — normal weekday schedule (6 AM – 8 PM, off overnight and weekends).
Schedule Manager — 24/7 schedule fault. Unit running all day, every day, including Sunday 1 AM.
Exception Schedule — holiday and one-time override entries. Check after events for forgotten overrides.
Point Attribute Report — no overrides. All points in Auto mode: a clean building baseline.
Point Attribute Report — Manual mode points highlighted. Run this before finalising any diagnosis.
Capstone Worksheet — blank. Students complete this with evidence from at least three simulator screens.
Capstone Worksheet — partially filled. Each section must reference a specific screen and evidence type.
Instructor Dashboard — scenario controls, capstone unlock, and class progress overview.
